map.string: Use CEF GPU shared-texture (accelerated paint) zero-copy path for browser media instead of CPU pixel readback/upload. Requires a viewer restart. (CEF daemon rework, on by default; falls back to CPU paint where the GPU interop is unavailable.)

Launch browser (CEF) media via the dedicated SLPluginCEF host, which statically links the CEF plugin instead of dlopen()ing it (avoids the Linux static-TLS crash; prerequisite for the sandbox). Requires a viewer restart. (CEF daemon rework, on by default.)
Enable the Chromium sandbox for CEF browser sub-processes (renderer/GPU/utility). Requires a viewer restart. (CEF daemon rework, on by default.)
Milliseconds per frame spent handing decoded meshes to the renderer. Any left over are carried to the next frame. Zero delivers one mesh per frame.

How the numeric keypad controls your avatar. 0 = behaves like the normal arrow keys; 1 = numpad moves the avatar when NumLock is off (types digits when on); 2 = numpad always moves the avatar regardless of NumLock (use if you have no NumLock key).

FAudio output device id (WASAPI device string on Windows, SDL device id elsewhere). Empty string uses the system default. Per-backend key so a saved id from one backend doesn't get mis-applied if the user switches engines.

OpenAL output device name (which also serves as its id — OpenAL doesn't surface a separate GUID). Empty string uses the system default. Per-backend key so a saved id from one backend doesn't get mis-applied if the user switches engines.

FMOD output device id (FMOD_GUID in canonical "{XXXXXXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX}" form). Empty string uses driver 0 / system default. Per-backend key so a saved id from one backend doesn't get mis-applied if the user switches engines.

FAudio backend: F3DAudio emitter InnerRadius in metres. Below this distance source channels diffuse to all speakers; above, clean directional pan. Applies live; new value is picked up on the next 3D update tick.

I3DL2 reverb preset applied by whichever audio backend supports reverb (FAudio always, OpenAL when ALC_EXT_EFX is present, FMOD always). PLAIN is the open-outdoor default; case-insensitive. Recognised: DEFAULT, GENERIC, PADDEDCELL, ROOM, BATHROOM, LIVINGROOM, STONEROOM, AUDITORIUM, CONCERTHALL, CAVE, ARENA, HANGAR, CARPETEDHALLWAY, HALLWAY, STONECORRIDOR, ALLEY, FOREST, CITY, MOUNTAINS, QUARRY, PLAIN, PARKINGLOT, SEWERPIPE, UNDERWATER, SMALLROOM. DEFAULT / SMALLROOM are mapped to backend-specific equivalents where the underlying preset table doesn't carry them by name. Applies live; preset changes are pushed to the engine on the next signal callback.

FAudio backend: reverb wet-send level. Scales F3DAudio's dsp.ReverbLevel per source before writing the per-source -> reverb-submix matrix. 0 disables reverb. The default (0.05) is intentionally subtle because the FAudioFX reverb tail is fairly pronounced at full strength. Applies live; picked up on the next update tick.

FAudio backend: enable the FAPOFX FXMasteringLimiter on the mastering voice. Prevents the device-side integer quantizer from clipping when many sources sum past unity in the float-internal mix (typical SL scenes with dozens of simultaneous sources). Disable only if you specifically want raw post-mix peaks, accepting the resulting distortion. Applies live; toggles the FAPO's enabled state without rebuilding the chain.

FAudio backend: gain-recovery time of the master limiter in milliseconds. FAPOFX range is [1, 20]; default 6. Lower = snappier release (more transparent on percussive material but can pump on sustained peaks); higher = smoother recovery at the cost of slightly attenuated transients after a hit. Applies live.

FAudio backend: master limiter loudness/threshold parameter. FAPOFX range is [1, 1800]; default 1000. Higher values leave more headroom before the limiter engages (less aggressive); lower values compress earlier (more aggressive). MSDN doesn't document the unit; treat as a subjective dial. Applies live.

OpenAL backend (EFX): reverb wet-send level, written directly to AL_EFFECTSLOT_GAIN on the auxiliary effect slot. 0 disables; range [0, 1]. The default (0.25) is higher than the FAudio key because the EFX slot-gain is a single global multiplier on the whole effect output rather than a per-source coefficient, so it needs less scaling to feel similarly "subtle". Applies live.

FMOD backend: reverb wet-send level, applied per channel via Channel::setReverbProperties on instance 0. Range [0, 1]; 0 disables. The default (0.15) sits between FAudio's per-source coefficient and OpenAL's slot-gain because FMOD's wet scalar interacts with the per-channel mix differently from either. Applies live.

Depth of the slow random-walk gain modulator applied by LLWindGen to the procedural wind drone. 0 disables gustiness entirely and the synth runs bit-identically to the historical steady drone. 1 means ±100% gain modulation, picked from a fresh random target every ~1.5 seconds and interpolated smoothly. Applies live across all reverb-capable backends; takes effect on the next synthesised wind sample.

Strength of the altitude-dependent gain lift applied to the wind drone when the camera is above water. 0 disables the boost entirely; 1 scales wind gain by up to 1.5x at the 4096m sim ceiling, following a square-root curve so the transition off the ground is perceptible without becoming overwhelming at typical skybox altitudes. The underwater muffle (cutoff drop + gain attenuation when the camera is submerged) is always on and not gated by this setting. Applies live; takes effect on the next coefficient update tick.

Reverse-Z depth buffering for greater depth precision at distance (float32 depth, near=1/far=0). Requires GL 4.5 or GL_ARB_clip_control; ignored (forward-Z) where unavailable, e.g. macOS GL 4.1. Change triggers a shader rebuild and GL buffer reallocation.

Allocate sun/spot shadow maps as 32-bit float depth instead of 24-bit fixed. Same storage size; trades uniform quantization for float precision (denser near the light's near plane). Reallocates the shadow buffers.

Sun/spot shadow PCF filter quality: 0 = Low (2x2, 1 gather), 1 = Medium (4x4, 4 gathers), 2 = High (6x6, 9 gathers), 3 = Ultra (PCSS contact-hardening: shadows sharpen near the contact point and soften with occluder distance, 17 gathers). Higher gives a wider, smoother penumbra at more texture fetches.

Ultra shadow tier only: converts the receiver-to-blocker depth gap into a penumbra radius in shadow texels. Higher = softer shadows further from the contact point. Requires AlchemyRenderShadowFilterQuality 3.
What tonemapper to use: 0 = Khronos Neutral, 1 = ACES Hill, 2 = ACES Boosted, 3 = Reinhard, 4 = Filmic, 5 = GT, 6 = AgX

Scopes floater: how many scopes are shown at once and how they are arranged. 0 = one filling the window, 1 = two side by side, 2 = two stacked, 3 = four in a grid. Which scope each pane shows is AlchemyScopePane0 through AlchemyScopePane3; right-click a pane to set it.

Scopes floater: which scope the first pane shows. 0 = RGB histogram, 1 = luminance, 2 = red, 3 = green, 4 = blue, 5 = vectorscope, 6 = waveform luminance, 7 = waveform RGB, 8 = parade. This is the pane a single-pane layout shows.
Scopes floater: which scope the second pane shows. Same values as AlchemyScopePane0. Used by the two-pane and four-pane layouts.
Scopes floater: which scope the third pane shows. Same values as AlchemyScopePane0. Used by the four-pane layout only.
Scopes floater: which scope the fourth pane shows. Same values as AlchemyScopePane0. Used by the four-pane layout only.
Scopes floater: plot histogram bins on a log scale so tall bins do not flatten the rest of the distribution onto the axis. 0 = linear.
Scopes floater: seconds between frame samples (0.1 = ten per second, which is about what hardware scopes run at). Lower costs more; 0 samples every frame. Only applies while a scopes floater is open.

Scopes floater: width in pixels of the point-sampled copy the histogram is measured from; height follows the world view's aspect. Range 32 to 1024. Raising it only reduces per-bin noise (which falls as 1/sqrt(samples)) at a linear cost in read-back and binning; 320 gives roughly 7 percent jitter per bin at 16:9.
Scopes floater: how far each sample moves the displayed histogram towards the new measurement, 0 to 1. 1 shows the raw sample and shimmers; lower settles but lags a change in the scene.

Upload strategy for the engine's shared uniform blocks: 0 = direct sub-updates per write, 1 = orphan and re-upload whole block per draw, 2 = stream through a shared ring buffer (unsynchronized map/unmap), 3 = stream through a persistently-mapped coherent ring (no per-draw map/orphan; falls back to 1 if buffer-storage is unavailable), 4 = persistently-mapped NON-coherent ring with explicit flush (often faster than 3 where coherent mappings are write-combined). Applies live; 2-4 avoid GPU sync stalls on drivers where buffer sub-updates are expensive (macOS).
Revoke permissions on object on sit(1), stand(2) or both(3)
Allows the agent to rez objects under the target locations land group. Must be a member of the land group.

Per-family UI font overrides. Map of font family name (e.g. SansSerif, Monospace) to override value. Override value is tried first as another family name from fonts.xml, then as a font filename. Empty/absent = built-in default. Applied at startup and on change without restart.
Enable chat keyword alerts for nearby chat and instant messages

Default skin tone applied to variant-capable emoji in the picker grid. -1 = no preference (yellow base); 0..4 = light, medium-light, medium, medium-dark, dark. Long-press or right-click an emoji to override on a single pick.

For COLRv1 emoji fonts that ship multiple CPAL palettes, pick the first palette flagged for dark backgrounds rather than the default (palette 0). Has no effect on COLRv0 / SVG / CBDT emoji fonts. Triggers a font reload on change.

Accent scripted objects on netmap in different colors.
Accent physical objects on netmap in different colors.
Accent temporary objects on netmap in different colors.

Multiplier for high-precision (smooth) mouse-wheel scroll and zoom speed: camera zoom, smooth list/container scrolling, minimap/world-map/preview zoom. 1.0 = default. Does not affect item steppers (spinners, menus, combo boxes).
Percentage of the window height that nearby chat toasts can appear in
Nearby chat toast offset from the bottom of the screen
Width of the nearby chat toasts (or 0 to have the toasts follow the width of the chat bar)
Name of the currently applied Lightbox Look; blank once settings drift from it
Name of the most recently applied Lightbox Look, kept for revert

Which avatar passes cast shadows. 0 = opaque only, 1 = opaque + alpha mask, 2 = full (also alpha blend). Lower values speed up crowd scenes by skipping the expensive alpha-blend avatar shadow pass across all cascades.

How sun shadow cascades are culled. 0 = cull and sort each cascade separately (default). 1 = cull and sort once against a frustum spanning all cascades, sharing the result (less CPU per frame, more GPU vertex work per cascade). Experimental.
Replace legacy glow with HDR bloom pyramid (pre-tonemap). 0 = legacy glow, 1 = HDR bloom.

Batch multiple materials into a single indexed draw call across the supported GLTF PBR and legacy material passes (opaque, alpha-mask, rigged, shadow, glow). 0 = one draw call per material (legacy), 1 = indexed multi-material batching. Reduces draw calls in material-heavy scenes.
HDR bloom luminance threshold in linear light. Values above this bloom; below, fall off softly via the knee. 1.0 = roughly "brighter than white".
Maximum radiance a single pixel may contribute to bloom. Bounds sub-pixel specular glints so they cannot become large flickering halos. Does not affect the sharp highlight in the scene itself.
Soft-knee width below the bloom threshold. Wider values give a softer, more gradual bloom onset. Range 0 to 1.
Number of bloom pyramid mip levels. More mips = wider, softer bloom. Clamped to [3, 7].

Base bloom pyramid resolution relative to scene. 0 = full, 1 = 3/4, 2 = half, 3 = quarter, 4 = eighth. Higher = faster and wider bloom reach per mip, with bilinear upscale at composite. Clamped to [0, 4].
Bloom upsample tent-filter radius multiplier. 1.0 = adjacent-texel taps. Values >1 widen the bloom per octave; >~2.5 starts to alias because the tent skips source texels.
Multiplier applied to alpha-tagged glow (legacy prim glow parameter) when fed into HDR bloom. Compensates for pre-tonemap composite so prim-glow halos match legacy brightness.

HDR bloom composite strength. Multiplies the final bloom pyramid before it is additively blended into the scene. Independent of RenderGlowStrength so HDR bloom and legacy glow can be tuned separately.

Enable the halation signal in HDR bloom. When off, the bloom pyramid allocates as R11F_G11F_B10F (half the bandwidth of RGBA16F) and skips the warmth extract and tinted composite. Requires RenderBloomHDR.
Photographic halation (warm halo around bright highlights). 0 disables. 0.25 is a gentle cinematic feel. Requires RenderBloomHalation.
Tint color for the halation halo (linear RGB). Default is a warm amber. Requires RenderBloomHalation.
Overall intensity of the chromatic aberration fringe. 0 disables the effect. 0.15 gives a subtle cinema lens feel; 0.5 is heavy. Range 0 to 1.
How quickly the aberration grows from the screen center outward. 1 is a linear ramp; higher values keep the center clean and push fringing to the edges. Range 0.5 to 4.
Rotates the red/blue split direction, in degrees. 0 is horizontal; 90 is vertical. Only meaningful when Anisotropy is nonzero. Range 0 to 360.
Stretches the fringe along the angle axis. 0 gives an even radial fringe; positive values elongate it into a directional smear for anamorphic-style aberration. Range -1 to 1.
Red channel horizontal offset direction. -1 shifts red inward on the X axis, +1 outward. Combined with RY for per-channel fringe direction. Range -1 to 1.
Red channel vertical offset direction. Pairs with OffsetRX. 0 keeps red split purely horizontal. Range -1 to 1.
Blue channel horizontal offset direction. Typically opposite sign of OffsetRX for a standard red/blue split. Range -1 to 1.
Blue channel vertical offset direction. Pairs with OffsetBX. 0 keeps blue split purely horizontal. Range -1 to 1.

Strength of the cross-screen (star) filter - the etched glass filter that diffracts every bright point in frame into a star. 0 disables. The arms carry a highlight's light spread along their length, so they are much dimmer than the core and this generally wants a large value - try 8 and work outward. Unlike the starburst under Lens Flare, which is locked to the sun, this streaks every highlight. Streaks ride on the bloom pyramid, so bloom strength 0 silences them. HDR only. Range 0 to 32.

Number of arms on each star. 4 is the classic cross filter, 6 and 8 match the denser gratings. Odd counts give an asymmetric star, since the arms are spread evenly rather than in opposed pairs. Range 2 to 12.
Rotation of the whole star in degrees, as if turning the filter in its thread. Range 0 to 360.

Spacing of the samples that build each arm, which sets how far the star reaches. 1.0 is the tuned value and gives a clean continuous streak; higher spreads the arms further, and lower draws them in tight. The range stops at 2 because beyond that the samples building each arm stop overlapping and the streak breaks up into a repeating lattice rather than getting longer. Length and falloff work together - a long streak with a fast falloff still fades out early, which is usually what reads best. Range 0.25 to 2.

How quickly each arm fades along its length, measured as how much brightness is lost between the core of a highlight and the tip of its arm. Low values give long even spokes; high values keep the star tight around the highlight. This changes only the shape of the arms - brightness belongs to Strength. Range 0.1 to 3.

Rainbow dispersion along the arms. A real star filter is a diffraction grating, and a grating separates wavelengths by angle, so the tips of the streaks go coloured while the core stays white. 0 gives clean white spokes. Range 0 to 1.

Strength of the lens dirt overlay - grime on the front element catching bloom and flare, the way a real lens lights up when something bright is in frame. 0 disables. 0.3 is a subtle used-lens feel; 1.0 is a filthy one. Only lights up where there is already bloom or flare to catch, so a flat scene stays clean no matter how high this goes. Range 0 to 2.
Which lens dirt plate to use. Greyscale images dropped into the user 'lensdirt' folder appear alongside the bundled ones and take priority over a bundled file of the same name. Leave empty for none.
How strongly bloom lights up the dirt. 0 means bloom passes through a clean lens; 1 is the full response. Raise it for hazy sunlit shots where the grime should catch everything. Range 0 to 2.

How strongly the lens flare lights up the dirt. 0 means the flare passes through a clean lens; 1 is the full response. This is the response that reads most like a real lens, since flare and grime share the same front element. Range 0 to 2.

Overall strength of the geometric lens distortion. 0 disables the effect entirely. 0.25 is a subtle wide-angle bend; 1.0 applies the shape coefficients in full. Only the world view is warped - nametags, selection outlines and UI are drawn afterwards and stay straight. Range 0 to 1.

Primary radial distortion coefficient. Negative values give barrel distortion (straight lines bow outward, the wide-angle look); positive values give pincushion (lines bow inward, common on telephoto). -0.2 is a mild wide angle, -0.4 approaches a fisheye look. Has no effect until Amount is raised. Range -0.5 to 0.5.

Secondary radial distortion coefficient, shaping the falloff toward the corners. Leave at 0 for a simple bend; small non-zero values reproduce the moustache distortion of real wide-angle lenses, where the bend reverses direction near the frame edge. Range -0.25 to 0.25.

Anamorphic desqueeze factor. 1.0 is a spherical lens and does nothing. 1.33 and 2.0 match the common anamorphic formats, stretching the image horizontally the way a desqueezed cinema frame looks. Range 0.5 to 2.5.

How the warped image is rescaled - 0 = none (pincushion can show black corners), 1 = fit (scaled so nothing ever goes black; the usual choice), 2 = fill (scaled so the whole undistorted frame stays visible, which can letterbox the corners)

[-0.5, 0.5] Offset of the optical axis from the frame center, x and y, z component unused. Non-zero values decenter the distortion the way a shifted or tilted lens does. Leave at zero for a centered lens.

[-0.05, 0.05] Brown-Conrady tangential (decentering) coefficients p1 and p2 in x and y, z component unused. These model a lens element mounted slightly off-axis and shear the image rather than bending it radially. Realistic values are tiny - below 0.01. Leave at zero unless deliberately faking a misaligned lens.
Name of image file for color grading LUT(TGA, PNG, or WebP)
Strength of the color grading LUT effect
Split toning strength for shadows and highlights. 0 disables the effect; 0.5 is a natural cinematic push. Tints shadows and highlights without shifting overall brightness.
Slides the midpoint between shadow and highlight tints. Negative values widen shadows (good for dark scenes); positive values widen highlights (good for bright scenes). Range -1 to 1.
Target color for shadow tones. Neutral gray (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) is identity. Try cool teal (0.35, 0.5, 0.55) for classic teal-and-orange looks.
Target color for highlight tones. Neutral gray (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) is identity. Try warm amber (0.6, 0.5, 0.4) to complement teal shadows.
Target color for midtones. Neutral gray (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) is identity. Warm tints like (0.55, 0.5, 0.45) flatter skin tones.
Midtone tint strength, independent from shadow/highlight amount. 0 disables; subtle values (0.15-0.35) add mood without muddying skin.

White balance temperature shift, in Kelvin relative to neutral daylight. Negative warms the image, positive cools it. Range -5000 to +5000. Default 0. Try -2500 tungsten glow, -1000 golden hour, +1500 blue hour, +3000 moonlit.

Green/magenta tint, perpendicular to the temperature axis. Negative pushes magenta, positive pushes green. Range -1 to +1. Default 0. Try -0.4 cyberpunk magenta, +0.4 fluorescent green, +0.75 Matrix green.

Shadow lift (R,G,B): adds to the darkest tones to raise the black floor and tint shadows. Per-channel range -0.5 to +0.5. Default (0,0,0). Try (0.02,0.02,0.05) cool shadow mist, (0.05,0.03,0) warm lift, negatives crush toward black.

Midtone gamma (R,G,B): bends the middle of the tonal range without moving blacks or whites. Above 1 brightens mids, below 1 darkens them. Per-channel range 0.5 to 1.5. Default (1,1,1). Try (1.1,1.1,1.1) open mids, (1.1,1.0,0.95) warm mids.

Highlight gain (R,G,B): multiplies the brightest tones to boost, clip, or tint whites. Per-channel range 0.5 to 1.5. Default (1,1,1). Try (1.05,1.02,0.95) warm highlights, (0.95,1.0,1.05) cool highlights, uniform <1 to tame blowouts.
Crushes values at or below this level to pure black. 0 is identity, 0.05 deepens blacks cinematically, 0.1+ starts clipping shadow detail.
Clips values at or above this level to pure white. 1 is identity, 0.95 blooms highlights, 0.9 produces a washed bleach-bypass look.
Shifts the whole image lighter or darker. Range -0.5 to 0.5; small values (±0.05) are already noticeable.
S-curve around midgray. 1 is identity; less than 1 flattens (matte film look), greater than 1 punches (values above 1.3 start clipping).
Recovers (negative) or boosts (positive) highlights without touching midtones. Use -0.3 to pull blown skies back from clipping.
Lifts (positive) or crushes (negative) shadows without touching midtones. Use +0.2 to reveal shadow detail in dark scenes.
Uniform saturation. 1 is identity, 0 is black-and-white, 1.2 is punchy, 1.5 is heavily stylized.
Smart saturation that pushes muted colors harder than already-saturated ones. Skin-friendly; range -1 to 1, 0.3 is a subtle lift.
Rotates all hues around the color wheel in degrees. Range -180 to 180. 30 warms everything; 180 is a full complement (inverted).
Per-channel filmic curve toe point (RGB). Pixels at or below this input level flatten toward black. Try (0.05, 0.05, 0.1) to lift shadow blues.
Per-channel filmic curve shoulder point (RGB). Pixels at or above this input level flatten toward white. Lower values (around 0.85) give a tighter roll-off.
Per-channel curve blend strength (RGB). 0 disables; 0.4 is typical film, differing values per channel create cross-process looks.
Color vision deficiency effect mode - 0 = off, 1 = protanopia (no L cones), 2 = deuteranopia (no M cones), 3 = tritanopia (no S cones)
[0, 1] Strength of applied color vision deficiency effect
Almost always want this true — animated dither is perceptually invisible, static dither can show as fixed grain.
Dither final screen output for 8 or 10-bit display to reduce banding artifacts on gradients, shadows, and sky

[0, 7] 0 = off, 1 = protanopia (no L cones), 2 = deuteranopia (no M cones), 3 = tritanopia (no S cones), 4 = Achromatopsia (rod monochromacy), 5 = Blue cone monochromacy (blue-tinted near-gray), 6 = Achromatomaly (severely reduced saturation), 7 = false-color exposure map

[0, 2] How a grabbed reference still is shown: 0 = off, 1 = wipe (still left of the seam, live right), 2 = side by side. Ignored unless a still has been grabbed. Session-scoped: a still does not outlive the session, so neither should the mode.
[0, 1] Where the wipe seam sits across the frame. Session-scoped, like RenderReferenceWipeMode.
[0, 1] Strength of applied film grain effect
Whether the film grain effect is animated between frames
[0, 1] luma position where grain peaks. 0 = shadows only, 0.5 = midtones (classic film), 1 = highlights only
Film grain effect style - 0 = mono luma, 1 = color (digital push), 2 = coarse (16mm feel), 3 = photon shot (CCD sensor)
color of the film grain. vec3(1) = neutral gray. Try vec3(1.0, 0.9, 0.8) for warm film grain, vec3(0.8, 0.9, 1.0) for cool video noise
Whether the focus point used for DoF is currently Locked in place
Allows the Depth of Field focus to actively follow the mouse point
Master intensity of the lens flare effect. 0 turns it off entirely; 1 is full strength. Use this as the on/off switch.
How far the horizontal anamorphic streak stretches across the screen. 0.5 reaches halfway; 1.0 crosses the full width. Range 0.01 to 2.
How quickly the streak fades toward its tips. Lower values leave a longer visible tail; higher values make the streak fade in close to the sun. Range 0.1 to 10.
Vertical thickness of the streak as a fraction of the screen. Lower is a thin hairline, higher is a soft horizontal band. Range 0 to 1.
Brightness multiplier for just the streak, separate from the master strength. 1 is neutral; higher boosts the streak without affecting the glow/ghosts. Range 0 to 5.
Color of the horizontal streak. The default cool blue mimics coated anamorphic cinema lenses; try warm tones for sci-fi or golden hour looks.
Red/blue color separation along the streak for a chromatic fringe look. 0 is clean; 1 gives a strong rainbow split. Range 0 to 1.
Size of the soft glow bloom directly around the sun. Small values hug the light; larger values create a wider halo of brightness. Range 0.01 to 0.5.
Softness of the central glow. Lower values give a gentle, spread-out bloom; higher values keep it tight and punchy. Range 1 to 30.
Intensity of the soft central glow around the sun. 0 disables the glow; 1 is neutral; higher boosts it. Range 0 to 5.
Number of lens ghost circles placed along the line from the sun through the screen center. Shape control only; use RenderLensFlareGhost to toggle the effect. Range 0 to 8.
Distance between consecutive ghosts. Smaller packs them near the sun; larger spreads them across the screen. Range 0.1 to 1.
Intensity of the lens ghost circles. 0 disables ghosts; 1 is neutral; higher boosts them. Range 0 to 5.
Radius of the halo ring that appears opposite the sun through screen center. Shape control only; use RenderLensFlareHalo to toggle the effect. Range 0.01 to 1.
Thickness of the halo ring. Smaller is a crisp hoop; larger is a soft diffuse ring. Range 0.01 to 0.5.
Intensity of the halo ring opposite the sun. 0 disables the halo; 1 is neutral; higher boosts it. Range 0 to 5.
Intensity of the starburst (diffraction-spike) pattern radiating from the sun, like aperture blades in a camera. 0 disables it. Range 0 to 5.
Number of aperture-like spikes in the starburst. Real cameras typically show 2x the blade count (6-blade = 12 spikes, etc). Range 1 to 32.
How crisp the starburst spikes look. Low values produce soft, wide rays; high values produce thin, needle-like beams. Range 1 to 256.
Length of the starburst spikes. 0 is short and tight to the sun; 1 lets them reach far across the screen. Range 0 to 1.
How wide the sun-occlusion test samples the scene depth. Larger values let thin geometry (foliage, wires) dim the flare more gracefully. Range 0.005 to 0.1.
Number of depth samples for sun-occlusion testing. Higher values give smoother partial occlusion transitions at a small performance cost. Range 1 to 32.

Whether to blur near camera in depth of field

Extra weight given to bright samples inside the defocus blur, which makes out-of-focus highlights read as distinct bokeh discs rather than a smooth blur. 0 is a plain average and is also the cheapest. 0.5 is a gentle lift; 2.0 is a strong cinematic pop. Range 0 to 4.

Brightness above which the highlight boost starts to apply. 0 boosts the whole range; raising it restricts the effect to genuine highlights and leaves midtones averaging normally. Only has an effect when Highlight Gain is above 0. Range 0 to 8.

Ceiling on how much radiance a single sample may contribute to a neighbouring bokeh disc. A specular glint can carry thousands of times the brightness of its surroundings; uncapped it spreads into a large blob that flickers as the camera moves. The in-focus pixel keeps its full intensity either way - only its contribution to the blur is capped. 0 disables the cap. Range 0 to 1024.

Number of aperture blades shaping the out-of-focus highlights. 0 gives the perfectly round bokeh of an idealised lens. 5 to 9 reproduce real diaphragms, where the discs become visible polygons - 6 is the most common on stills lenses. Values below 3 are treated as circular. Range 0 to 11.
Rotation of the aperture polygon in degrees. Only has an effect when Aperture Blades is 3 or more. Range 0 to 360.

Rounds the aperture blades back toward a circle. 0 gives hard straight-edged polygons; 1 is fully round, matching a rounded diaphragm held wide open. Only has an effect when Aperture Blades is 3 or more. Range 0 to 1.

Stretches out-of-focus highlights into ovals, the way the cylindrical element of an anamorphic lens does. 1.0 is a round spherical-lens disc. Above 1 gives taller-than-wide ovals, the classic anamorphic signature; below 1 gives wider-than-tall. The stretch preserves area, so this changes the shape of the blur without changing how strong it is. Range 0.25 to 4.

Optical vignetting, also called cat's eye. Toward the frame edges the lens barrel clips the aperture, squeezing round bokeh into lens-shaped slivers that lean away from the centre while the middle of the frame stays round. 0 disables. 0.3 is a natural fast-prime look; 0.7 is heavy. Range 0 to 1.

Longitudinal chromatic aberration - the colour cast real glass leaves on the rim of an out-of-focus highlight, which flips hue either side of the focal plane. 0 disables. 0.2 is a subtle uncorrected-lens feel; 0.6 is strong. This is separate from the frame-wide fringe under Chromatic Aberration, which appears whether or not anything is defocused. Range 0 to 1.
Colour cast on highlights in front of the focal plane. The default light magenta matches the usual signature of uncorrected glass; swap with the far tint to reverse the effect.
Colour cast on highlights behind the focal plane. The default light green is the counterpart to the near tint; a real lens shifts hue in opposite directions either side of focus.
